geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the cantilever with a continuous bar logic so the primary mass can read as one coherent street-building body instead of a generic block.
Tune the dominant bar to remain compact while establishing clearer horizontal continuity.
Add a courtyard void tied to the dominant mass so the ground threshold becomes legible and public.
Make the carved space substantial enough to count as usable public open space.
Open the court toward the verified access side to strengthen the public threshold.
Make the new courtyard wrapper the root so the dominant mass remains in the ancestry while the public void governs the composition.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant mass from a boxy cantilever into a more continuous, site-responsive bar with clearer ground engagement and a less generic silhouette.
Pull the dominant gesture toward a more legible horizontal continuity so the mass reads as one primary building body rather than a stacked block.
Add a clearer public void so the ground edge can read as a usable threshold rather than a shallow surface notch.
Keep the carved space substantial enough to be read as a public court/terrace and not decorative subtraction.
Align the void to the verified access side so the street threshold becomes explicit and programmatically legible.
Preserve the long-axis ordering while letting the new void and bend operation organize a clearer dominant/support hierarchy.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact two-level block with a small horizontal cut, but the massing is still mostly boxy and the apparent void is shallow rather than a clearly public courtyard, undercut, or entry seam. Across views it is coherent, so it avoids the worst cross-view collision problem, and the parcel fit is generally contained. However, the dominant gesture is not strongly tied to the west-oriented public threshold implied by the program context and the verified access edge; the road response feels more like a side notch than an active ground address. The section is also underdeveloped for neighborhood living: there is no convincing inhabited terrace or meaningful public ground figure, so the program semantics read weaker than the silhouette. The result is more like a generic stacked mass with a clipped slot than a capacity-aware street building with a legible public edge.
